metas.name: Agriculture - Banana
metas.note: Banana plants are found around the city of Alanya.

metas.name: Agriculture - Cotton
metas.note: Cotton is mainly found in the region surrounding the city of Şanlıurfa.

metas.name: Agriculture - Greenhouse
metas.note: If you find yourself surrounded by greenhouses, you are likely to be along the south coast west of Adana.

metas.name: Agriculture - Olive
metas.note: Olive trees are mainly found on the Mediterranean coast.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.note: Sunflowers are mainly found in northwestern Turkey.

metas.name: Agriculture - Tea
metas.note: Tea plantations are common in the province of Rize.

metas.name: Agriculture - Vineyard
metas.note: A majority of all vineyards in Turkey can be found in a region east of Izmir.

metas.name: Architecture - Bodrum Architecture
metas.note: Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue details or unpainted stone walls.

metas.name: Architecture - Flat Roof
metas.note: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.

metas.name: Architecture - Metal Roof
metas.note: Metal roofs are most common in the east.

metas.name: Architecture - Pyramid Metal Roof
metas.note: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.

metas.name: Architecture - Sandstone
metas.note: Many buildings in the Nevşehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

metas.name: Architecture - Tiled Roof
metas.note: Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.

metas.name: Car Meta - Truck Coverage
metas.note: Generation 4 truck coverage is mainly found in the far east of the country and along the southern coast, with smaller pockets in the west and around Kastamonu.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - D525 south of Söke
metas.note: Road D525 south of Söke is a completely straight road going south-south-west to north-north-east with winter Generation 3 coverage. Along the road you will typically find a large amount of reed.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - E99 south of Sanliurfa
metas.note: Road E99 south of Şanlıurfa is a divided highway which can be recognised by the slightly hazy Generation 4 sunrise coverage combined with the flat agricultural landscape and general south-north road angle.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bozcaada Tourist Sign
metas.note: These light blue and grey touristic signs which are either arrow shaped or rectangular with a half circle on the top can be found on the island of Bozcaada.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chevron - Yellow on Black
metas.note: Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the Balıkesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chevron Black on Yellow
metas.note: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir.

metas.name: Infrastructure - European Poleplate
metas.note: In the European part of Turkey, except Istanbul, utility poles, and other electrical infrastructure, will have a 6 digit code, which is often seen on a small pole plate under the yellow electricity warning plate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Highway without Divider
metas.note: Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Red Oval Sign
metas.note: Street signs in Trabzon and Yalvaç are red and oval-shaped. House numbers also feature the same design.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsign - Ankara
metas.note:
Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.

Beware that some newer street signs are red.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsign - Bolu
metas.note: Street signs in Bolu are also green, but are completely flat and lack any kind of border.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsign - Bursa
metas.note:
Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

NOTE: Several other types of infrastructure in Bursa, such as fences and guardrails, may also be coloured green.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsign - Istanbul
metas.note:
Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsign - Izmir
metas.note: Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Watertank - Horizontal on top of Vertical
metas.note: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to Elâzığ.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Watertank - Octagonal
metas.note: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from İskenderun to Sanliurfa.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Watertank - Spherical
metas.note: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Watertank - Vertical
metas.note: Vertical water tanks can be found in most of Turkey, but are notably uncommon along the south and west coast.

metas.name: Landscape - Cliff Valley
metas.note: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.

metas.name: Landscape - Göreme Monoliths
metas.note: Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

metas.name: Landscape - Grassland
metas.note: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

metas.name: Landscape - Lake Beysehir
metas.note: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

metas.name: Landscape - Lake Egirdir
metas.note: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

metas.name: Landscape - Lake Van
metas.note: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.

metas.name: Landscape - Lush
metas.note: Northern Turkey tends to be significantly lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.

metas.name: Landscape - Mount Ararat
metas.note: Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.

metas.name: Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.note: Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.

metas.name: Vegetation - Turkish Pine
metas.note:
Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

NOTE: Turkish pines can appear very similar to Aleppo pines, which are uncommon in Turkey, but are often found in other Mediterranean countries.
